conventions.title: A feature’s callout is `<folder>-callout.tsx` with `<folder>-callout-illustration.svg`
conventions.description: A folder’s illustrated callout is named after the folder (`logs/logs-callout.tsx` + `logs-callout-illustration.svg`). Extra callouts in a folder that already has its own, like `performance/backend-callout.tsx`, are fine. Found by Claude in `sites/`.

conventions.title: A default export is named after its file
conventions.description: `site-plan-card.tsx` default-exports `SitePlanCard` (or a qualified `SitesSitePlanCard`); `site-plan-card/index.tsx` does too. Matching names make components greppable from either side.

conventions.title: A hook lives in `use-<hook-name>.ts`
conventions.description: A module whose only runtime export is a hook is named after it in kebab-case (`useSitePlan` → `use-site-plan.ts`), and a `use-*.ts` file exports the hook its name promises.

conventions.title: File and folder names are kebab-case
conventions.description: Every directory and file name (before its extensions) is lower-case kebab-case, e.g. `site-settings/use-site-plan.ts`.

conventions.title: Component props types are `<Component>Props`
conventions.description: An exported component whose props use a named type calls that type `<ComponentName>Props`. Inline object types are left alone.

conventions.title: Test files end in `.test.ts(x)`
conventions.description: A file in a `test/` folder that contains `describe`/`it`/`test` blocks is named `*.test.ts` or `*.test.tsx`. Unsuffixed files in `test/` are then reserved for fixtures and helpers.

conventions.title: A test file is named after the module it tests
conventions.description: `foo/test/bar.test.tsx` tests `foo/bar.tsx` (or `foo/bar/`), and `foo/test/index.test.tsx` tests `foo/index.tsx`. A test whose name matches nothing next to its `test/` folder is hard to find from the code it covers.

conventions.title: `.tsx` only for files that contain JSX
conventions.description: Files without JSX use the `.ts` extension, so the extension tells you whether a module renders anything.

conventions.title: Code is TypeScript, not JavaScript
conventions.description: Source and test files use `.ts` / `.tsx`, never `.js` / `.jsx`, so everything is type-checked. Tool config files such as `eslint.config.mjs` are exempt.

conventions.title: An upsell illustration is `upsell-illustration.svg`
conventions.description: A folder with one upsell image calls it plain `upsell-illustration.svg` (or `.tsx`); the folder already says what it’s for. Found by Claude in `sites/`.

conventions.title: A folder’s utils module is `utils.ts`, not `<folder>-utils.ts`
conventions.description: Per-folder utility modules are plain `utils.ts(x)`. Repeating the folder name (`storage/storage-utils.ts`) adds nothing; topical prefixes that don’t repeat it (`contact-validation-utils.ts`) are fine. Found by Claude in `sites/`.

conventions.title: Shared functions go in `utils`, not `helpers`
conventions.description: Grab-bag modules are called `utils.ts` or `utils/` (17 files, 6 folders today) rather than `helpers`, `helper` or `util`.

conventions.title: A modal folder’s body component is `content-info.tsx`
conventions.description: In `*-modal/` folders, the modal body that dataviews actions lazy-load without the `Modal` chrome is `content-info.tsx` (3 folders: `site-leave-modal`, `site-reset-modal`, `site-restore-modal`; the `-content-info.tsx` suffix is also used in `hosting-feature-activation-modal` and `migration-overview`). `site-change-address-modal` calls the same role `content.tsx`. One name makes the lazy-import targets predictable.
